candidates.label: geoCovers
candidates.comment: A geo covers relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place completely covers another, meaning every point of the covered entity is within the covering entity. Also called: covers, encompasses, overlies. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo covers "City 'Paris'", "North America" geo covers "Lake 'Superior'", "City 'Springfield'" geo covers "House '123 Main St'". Distinct from geoCoveredBy, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: spatial
candidates.comment: A general spatial relation between a creative work and a place, used when more specific location properties are not applicable. Also called "related to place", "takes place in", "associated location", "geographic context". Examples: "The novel has spatial Paris", "The painting's spatial is a rural landscape", "This document's spatial is the Amazon rainforest.". Distinct from spatialCoverage, which indicates the specific geographic focus of the content.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: longitude
candidates.comment: A longitude relation between geographic coordinates or a place and its longitudinal value. Also called: geographic longitude, east-west coordinate, meridian position. Examples: "Eiffel Tower longitude 2.2945", "Statue of Liberty longitude -74.0445", "Mount Everest longitude 86.9250".

candidates.label: geoIntersects
candidates.comment: A geo intersects relation representing a spatial relationship where two geometries or places share at least one common point. Also called: overlaps with, touches, crosses. Examples: "River 'Thames'" geo intersects "City 'London'", "Road 'Main Street'" geo intersects "Park 'Central Park'", "Country 'USA'" geo intersects "Country 'Canada'". Distinct from geoDisjoint, which has no points in common.

candidates.label: locationCreated
candidates.comment: A creation location relation between a creative work and the place where it was created. Also called: place of creation, origin location, created in. Examples: "Painting locationCreated Paris", "Novel locationCreated London", "Film locationCreated Hollywood". Distinct from location, which refers to the current or general location of an entity.

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: regionDrained
candidates.comment: A region drained relation between a lymphatic vessel or vein and the anatomical structure or system from which it removes fluid. Also called drains region, supplies drainage to. Examples: "The femoral vein drains region 'the leg'.", "A lymphatic vessel drains region 'the arm'.", "The hepatic portal vein drains region 'the digestive tract'."

candidates.label: departureTerminal
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a flight and its departure terminal identifier. Also called: terminal number, flight terminal, departure building. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure terminal "Terminal 5", "Flight UA123" departure terminal "Terminal 3". Distinct from arrivalTerminal, which is the arrival terminal.

candidates.label: departureStation
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a train trip and the station from which it departs. Also called: origin train station, departure rail station, train departure point. Examples: "Train to Paris" departure station "London St Pancras International", "Commuter Train" departure station "Grand Central Terminal". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is the destination station.

chosen_property.label: occurredDuring
chosen_property.definition: An event that occurred during another event.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property fits the Event → Event signature for nested temporal events.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: duringMedia
candidates.comment: A during media relation between a how-to direction and a media object or URL representing the circumstances while performing this direction. Also called "instructional media", "step-by-step video", "visual guide". Examples: "How-to direction 'Attach part A' duringMedia 'Video of assembly'", "Direction 'Stir mixture' duringMedia 'Image of stirring technique'".

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: byMonth
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the month(s) of the year on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "months of year", "monthly recurrence", "in month". Examples: "Annual conference schedule byMonth 10", "Quarterly report schedule byMonth 3,6,9,12".

candidates.label: byMonthDay
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for a schedule, indicating the day(s) of the month on which a recurring event occurs. Also called "day of month", "monthly day recurrence", "on day of month". Examples: "Rent payment schedule byMonthDay 1", "Board meeting schedule byMonthDay 15".

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

chosen_property.label: occurredBefore
chosen_property.definition: An event that occurred before another event.
chosen_property.justification: No schema.org property fits the Event → Event signature for preceding events.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: earlyPrepaymentPenalty
candidates.comment: An early prepayment penalty relation between a repayment specification and a monetary amount, representing the fee for paying off a loan ahead of schedule. Also called "prepayment fee", "early payoff penalty", "exit fee". Examples: "Mortgage repayment earlyPrepaymentPenalty '$500'", "Loan agreement earlyPrepaymentPenalty '2% of remaining balance'", "Car loan earlyPrepaymentPenalty '$100'".

candidates.label: nextItem
candidates.comment: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: dateVehicleFirstRegistered
candidates.comment: A temporal registration relation between a vehicle and the date of its first registration with public authorities. Also called: first registration date, initial registration, vehicle registration date. Examples: "Car" date vehicle first registered "2018-03-15", "Motorcycle" date vehicle first registered "2020-07-01", "Truck" date vehicle first registered "2015-11-20".
